findings.title: findMany is removed without migrating production callers
findings.body: The public findMany method is replaced by getBaseConditions, and getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions now return Prisma.Sql instead of Prisma WhereInput objects. The PR changes only this service and its test, with no production caller migrated to $queryRaw with getBaseConditions. Any existing caller using service.findMany or passing the returned conditions into a Prisma where clause will fail TypeScript compilation; all such call sites must be migrated in this PR or a compatibility adapter retained.

findings.title: Event-type filter returns an unparenthesized OR fragment
findings.body: When eventTypeId is the only filter, buildFilterConditions returns `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)` without outer parentheses. If a caller composes it naturally as `WHERE ${authConditions} AND ${filterConditions}`, PostgreSQL precedence parses it as `(auth AND eventTypeId = ...) OR (eventParentId = ...)`, allowing the eventParentId branch to bypass the authorization conditions. getBaseConditions happens to wrap the fragment, but the public getFilterConditions result no longer guarantees the grouping that the previous Prisma WhereInput object provided; the predicate itself should be wrapped in parentheses.

findings.title: Team and org raw SQL branches are never executed against the database
findings.body: The org and team authorization tests only compare Prisma.Sql objects constructed with the same template helper as the implementation, while the sole $queryRaw execution in the suite uses user scope with scalar userId/teamId predicates. The `= ANY(array)` bindings and `"isTeamBooking"` predicates used exclusively by team/org scopes are therefore never sent to PostgreSQL, so invalid array-parameter encoding, column names, or SQL syntax would pass these tests and fail only at runtime. Add $queryRaw execution tests for team and org scopes.

findings.title: Public options type loses discriminated-union type safety
findings.body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for every scope, replacing the previous discriminated union that required teamId exactly when scope is "team". A call site such as { scope: "team", userId, orgId } now compiles, fails zod validation inside the constructor, and silently yields the 1=0 condition for every query, turning a programming error into an empty insights result instead of a compile-time error. Keep the discriminated union for typed callers or make untrusted-input handling explicit.

findings.title: Caching tests are deleted while caching logic remains
findings.body: The PR deletes the Caching describe block, but InsightsBookingService still maintains cachedAuthConditions and cachedFilterConditions and returns those cached Prisma.Sql objects on subsequent calls. No remaining test verifies that a second call reuses the cached conditions instead of rebuilding them and repeating the membership/team database queries. Restore caching coverage, for example by asserting repeated calls return the identical object, or remove the caching logic intentionally.
